title: A Confession for the Letter
premise: Retired detective Jude Nakamura, hiding from a past case that ruined him behind the shelves of his failing bookshop, is pulled back in when a missing woman's diary arrives anonymously—its entries continuing weeks past her disappearance. As Jude deciphers the coded confessions hidden in the diary's margins, he realizes the woman staged her own vanishing to escape a family inheritance built on a decades-old murder: the very case that ended his career. The trail leads to an anniversary dinner where her family will toast her memory, forcing Jude to choose between exposing the truth and protecting the one person who once saved his life. In the end, Jude delivers the confession to its intended recipient—the missing woman herself—and lets her decide whether survival is worth the price of silence.
about_author: Dominic Whitlock spent fifteen years as a court stenographer before turning to fiction, transcribing thousands of testimonies that taught him how truth hides inside ordinary sentences. He writes from a coastal town where fog rolls in earlier than anyone admits.

chapters.title: The Diary That Outlived Her
chapters.summary: Jude Nakamura's POV. A brown-paper parcel arrives at Whitlock's Books containing Mara Voss's diary—officially closed as a drowning three years ago. The final entry is dated eleven days after her death. Jude's quiet dread gives way to the old detective reflex he swore off; the emotional beat is reluctant awakening, the pull of a puzzle that refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: Margins Written in Code
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with diary excerpts in Mara's voice. Deciphering the marginal cipher, Jude finds Mara documenting threats from within her own family over the Voss inheritance—and a name she never wrote out, only circled. He visits the grieving brother, Elliot, whose grief curdles into warning. The beat deepens: loyalty to an old friend who begged Jude to let this case die, versus the truth pulling him forward.

chapters.title: A Toast to the Missing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV infiltrating the Voss anniversary dinner under a caterer's borrowed jacket. Confronted by Elliot, Jude realizes the circled name was his own—Mara trusted only him to follow. Elliot confesses he helped stage her disappearance to free her from the family's murderous legacy, but someone else at the table has been reading the same diary pages. Climactic tension: the toast is raised, and a guest quietly leaves to intercept the parcel's sender.

chapters.title: Confession for the Letter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, closing with Mara's letter read aloud. Racing the interceptor to a coastal cottage, Jude finds Mara alive, having mailed the diary deliberately—to force the truth into daylight on her terms. He delivers her confession to the assembled family and police, ending the inheritance's curse but costing her the anonymity she bought. Resolution: Jude reopens his bookshop sign, no longer hiding, as Mara chooses testimony over survival in silence.
